page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by the Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with one thread per core, providing a total of 16 vCPUs. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 11469.52 and a PassMark CPU score of 14861.27. However, single-core processing is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1150.39. Memory read bandwidth is average, reaching 834.57 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 54.29 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though large block write bandwidth is weak at 24.73 GB/sec. The server handles database operations and web serving at average tiers, achieving 12.97 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 10.85 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. LLM inference speeds are average for small 135M models but drop to weak levels for medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.cm4.4xlarge offers a balanced resource density of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU, typical of general-purpose hardware classes. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs reduces overhead for workloads that rely on network-attached storage and do not require hardware acceleration. Given the average multi-core performance and moderate network bandwidth, this instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, Redis caching, and moderate database operations.
